subject: Regional residency and VPC keystore snapshot for Medistra pilot
messages:
From: Kelsey Turner <kelsey.turner@medistra.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@medistra.com>, SecurityOps <security@medistra.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Residency confirmation + VPC controls for Medistra pilot

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To move our pilot forward we need a short, written confirmation of the hosting and network controls so our security and procurement teams can close scope. Specifically:

- Can you confirm the pilot will be hosted only in EU regions (we are targeting eu-central-1) and that no customer data will egress to other regions?
- For private connectivity: do you support PrivateLink / VPC peering and can you describe the operator access model?
- Keystore: can you provide a snapshot of key custody options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed) and whether HSM-backed keys are available for this configuration?
- We also need a pointer to SIG / CAIQ / SOC 2 artifacts or a short packet we can attach to our vendor security review.

Target: receive confirmation + artifacts by EOD Oct 6 so our procurement can include the environment in the SOW.

Appreciate a concise summary we can circulate.

Best,
Kelsey Turner
Director, Security & Privacy
Medistra Health

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Turner <kelsey.turner@medistra.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 16:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + VPC controls for Medistra pilot

Hi Kelsey —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front, followed by details and attachments.

1) Region residency: We can commit the pilot to EU-only hosting in eu-central-1. All compute and persistent storage for the pilot will be provisioned in that region. We will not replicate or failover data to non-EU regions unless you request it in writing.

2) Private connectivity: Redwood supports two deployment patterns for private access: (a) VPC peering / PrivateLink to a Private Deployment (recommended), or (b) Dedicated: reserved capacity with private peering. Operator access is restricted to named operator roles and must be enabled per-customer; by default operator actions require break-glass approval and are logged. Networking flow: customer VPC <-> privatelink endpoint in eu-central-1, with SCP/route-table controls on your side.

3) Keystore options: we support customer-managed KMS (recommended) with the option to use a customer HSM (BYOK into an HSM-backed key). Redwood-managed keys are available but can be scoped to EU-only HSM clusters if required. See attached keystore snapshot for current operator separation and rotation cadence.

4) Artifacts: attaching a compact runbook that contains the residency statement, peering topology, operator ACL template, and references to our CAIQ/SIG index and SOC 2 report download instructions.

Attachments included: residency-runbook.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB), keystore-inventory.csv (CSV, 34KB)

Next steps I recommend: 30-minute triage call with Security + Infra to validate the peering diagram and confirm KMS flow. Jordan, can you propose times?

If you want this formatted into a short memo for procurement I can produce one that can be appended to the SOW.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Turner <kelsey.turner@medistra.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + VPC controls for Medistra pilot

Hi all —

Adding the keystore & SOC2 bridge artifacts Naomi here (ops/security). Notes below and attached a short bridge playbook.

- Keystore snapshot: the attached CSV lists active key aliases, region binding (eu-central-1), key owner scope (customer-managed vs redwood-managed), and most recent rotation date. We currently operate an HSM-backed cluster in eu-central-1 that can be dedicated by contract for high-assurance customers.
- Operator separation: operators do not have direct KMS access to customer-managed keys; our control plane orchestrates usage via short-lived credentials and does not persist plaintext keys. Audit logs for all KMS operations are available and can be delivered as part of the evidence pack.
- SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ: we maintain a CAIQ index and a SOC 2 report (redacted) behind an access link. I included a short SOC2 bridge playbook outlining what to expect in the evidence package and a checklist for what medistra will need to validate the custody model.

Attachments included: soc2-bridgeplaybook.docx (DOCX, 160KB)

If you want an HSM-binding addendum or a signed keystore SLA, we can scope it in the DPA.

—Naomi Feldman
Staff, Security Operations (Redwood Inference)
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + VPC controls for Medistra pilot

I can take the ops side for the triage call. Proposed slots (CET): Oct 4 09:00-09:30, Oct 4 15:00-15:30, Oct 5 10:00-10:30. Please pick one and I will lock a calendar invite and draft an agenda:
- Confirm peering diagram and IP ranges

- Evidence handoff: SOC2 redacted report, CAIQ index location, KMS audit log snapshot

We will also prepare a one-page procurement memo that summarizes the region commitment and operator access model for inclusion in the SOW if that helps procurement close.

Kelsey
